expr: (list (compare-strings "abc" nil nil "abc" nil nil) (compare-strings "abc" nil nil "abd" nil nil) (compare-strings "xabc" 1 nil "abc" nil nil) (compare-strings "abc" 1 2 "abc" 1 2) (compare-strings "" nil nil "" nil nil) (compare-strings "" nil nil "a" nil nil))
note: NIL BOUNDS AND AN OFFSET START, the two shapes s.el actually passes: `s-ends-with?' calls (compare-strings suffix nil nil s start-pos nil ignore-case), so a nil START means 0, a nil END means the string's length, and a non-zero START compares a SUFFIX of the second string against the whole of the first. Emacs answers (t -3 t t t -1). The last two elements are the empty-string corners the index arithmetic has to survive: two empty spans are `t', and an empty span against a non-empty one is -1, which is -(1+0). kg answers `void-function' at this pin.
